title: platform-standup-2026-03-12
content:
Date: 2026-03-12
Attendees: Asha Patel (owner), Miguel Santos, Priya Desai, Liam O'Connor, Hannah Kim, remote: Zoe Ramos
Duration: 25m

Purpose: Weekly platform standup focused on control plane changes, routing behavior, auth tokens, and quota enforcement. Quick sync + blockers and action items for the week.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Control plane: Canary for API router v3.2 started; first canary showed spike in 99p latency for multi-tenant path -> rolled back to canary 1. We have a fix in PR 834 that limits header processing on hot path.
- Routing: Smart routing config updated to prefer regional pools for EU customers; need one more compatibility test for older model variants.
- Auth: Short-lived service tokens rollout on staging; one issue where refreshs failed during high concurrency (PLAT-472).
- Quotas: Enforcement bug causing soft-quotas to not throttle when burst window exceeded; root cause identified, mitigation deployed to staging; affected dedicated customers saw 503s last night.

Notes by area:

1) Control Plane
- Update: Canary deployment of api-router v3.2 started 2026-03-10 across 5% traffic. Observed increase in p99 latency for /v1/generate when request header count > 12 (multi-tool calls).
- Investigation: Miguel triaged and found additional per-request header parsing added a synchronous validation step. This interacts poorly with our continuous-batching path and increases context-switching.
- Action: PR #834 (linked) adds async header parsing and moves legacy header checks off hot path. Staging results positive: p50/p95 unchanged, p99 back to baseline.
- Next steps: Run extended canary with 10% traffic for two days after merging PR 834. If stable, schedule rollout to prod on 2026-03-15 with rollback window.
- Owner: Miguel Santos (lead), Asha to coordinate rollout schedule with SRE.

2) Routing / Smart routing
- Update: Regional preference switch for EU routing enabled. This should reduce cross-region egress and lower latency for EU customers.
- Outstanding test: Some older model variants (llama-70b-int8) don't advertise a compatible kv-cache layout, causing fallback to global pool.
- Action: Priya to run compatibility matrix tests for top 10 customer model pins and create compatibility shims where necessary. Expected completion: 2026-03-14.
- Note: Added route metric to signal when fallback/global pool is used; will emit alert if fallback rate > 1% for > 15m.

3) Auth / Tokens
- Update: Short-lived service tokens (15m default TTL) are on staging. This reduces blast radius of leaked credentials.
- Incident: PLAT-472 reports token refresh failures under high concurrency from internal batch job. Root cause: token cache stampede on auth service.
- Mitigation: Implemented jitter and singleflight in staging, added circuit breaker for auth service to surface degraded auth with 429 instead of 500.
- Action: Liam to add load test simulating 200 concurrent refreshes and confirm metrics; expected by 2026-03-13.

4) Quotas / Rate limiting
- Issue: Several dedicated customers observed 503s between 03:10-03:40 UTC on 2026-03-11. Investigation shows soft-quota enforcement path did not cap burst-window correctly leading to quota plugin throwing unhandled error.
- Root cause: Regression introduced in PLAT-489 where a nil-check was removed in quota evaluation. Fix added back the guard and added unit tests for burst-window edge cases.
- Status: Fix deployed to staging and hotfix branch created for prod. Hannah preparing a hotfix deploy; target prod deploy 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC with on-call and rollback plan.
- Customer impact: CS alerted customers with summary; account managers prepping detailed postmortems.

5) Observability / Metrics
- New: Added per-route token-level cost breakdown dashboard to console; still in beta for internal testing.
- Alerting: Added p99 increase alert for api-router when header-count > 10. Current threshold tuned based on staging numbers.

Blockers / Risks:
- Canary rollback risk if PR 834 introduces edge-case for older clients (API clients with malformed header ordering). Need compatibility tests.
- Auth stampede mitigation needs load validation before short-lived tokens can go prod.
- Quota hotfix timing: deploy tonight needs 4hr observation window; may impact scheduled Dedicated maintenance windows.

Action items (owner / due)
- Miguel: Merge PR #834 after signoff, run 10% extended canary (due 2026-03-13).
- Priya: Run routing compatibility matrix for top 10 model pins; report (due 2026-03-14).
- Liam: Load test auth refresh at 200 concurrent refreshes; publish results (due 2026-03-13).
- Hannah: Prepare and execute quota hotfix prod deploy, coordinate with on-call and CS (deploy 2026-03-12 22:00 UTC).
- Asha: Draft customer-facing incident summary for quota 503s and share with CS for approval (due 2026-03-13).

Decisions made:
- Postpone global rollout of api-router v3.2 until PR 834 validated in extended canary.
- Short-lived tokens will remain on staging until auth load tests pass; no prod cutoff scheduled yet.

Open questions:
- Do we need to support legacy header ordering in clients, or should we publish a breaking-change notice? (Tentative: prefer shim for 2 weeks then deprecate.)
- Should we tighten fallback alerts threshold from 1% to 0.5%? Priya to recommend after compatibility tests.

Follow-ups / Next meeting:
- Quick sync Wednesday 2026-03-14 (15m) to review canary and compatibility tests.
- Full platform weekly on Friday to review progress and customer impact.

Links & references:
- PLAT-472: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-472
- PLAT-489: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-489
- PR #834: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/834
- Control plane design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Control+Plane+Design+Notes

Notes to self:
- Add more synthetic tests for header-heavy requests to nightly pipeline.
- Remind SRE to extend logs retention for quota plugin traces for 48h after deploy.

End of notes.
